eyebrow: Quantum Error Correction & Fault Tolerance · Chapter 3
subtitle: Lesson 11 · Quantum Error Correction Basics

eyebrow: The trick: do everything in the Hadamard basis

steps.label: Z|+⟩ = |−⟩ and Z|−⟩ = |+⟩
steps.sub: A phase-flip swaps |+⟩,|−⟩ exactly like a bit-flip swaps |0⟩,|1⟩

steps.label: Not a coincidence — the X/Z basis duality
steps.sub: It lets you rotate the bit-flip code's entire construction

steps.label: Apply a Hadamard to the data qubit first
steps.sub: Then run the identical two-CNOT encoding circuit

steps.label: A Z error now flips a qubit between |+⟩ and |−⟩
steps.sub: Exactly mirroring how X flipped |0⟩ and |1⟩ in the bit-flip code

steps.label: X1X2 and X2X3 catch disagreements in the Hadamard basis
steps.sub: Where the bit-flip code's Z1Z2, Z2Z3 caught computational-basis disagreements

steps.label: Both read +1 on the valid encoded states
steps.sub: And flip to −1 exactly when a Z error has hit one of the 3 qubits

code:
Error location   State    Syndrome (X1X2,X2X3)   Correction
None              000      00                      none needed
Qubit 1           100      10                      apply Z to qubit 1
Qubit 2           010      11                      apply Z to qubit 2
Qubit 3           001      01                      apply Z to qubit 3
caption: Structurally identical to the bit-flip code's table — X error/flip replaced by Z error/apply-Z, because the bases are perfectly swapped.

steps.label: An X error leaves both X1X2 and X2X3 unchanged
steps.sub: They commute with X errors — the syndrome reads 00 regardless

steps.label: Neither 3-qubit code alone is general-purpose
steps.sub: Each protects against exactly one error type

steps.label: Combining both ideas handles an arbitrary error
steps.sub: Not picking one — that's exactly what the next lesson builds

subtitle: Concatenate both codes correctly, and get protection against any single-qubit error.
